scope: Principal cast and recurring supporting people across the play; opening-scene references. Source binding and full reference inventory pending.

cards.name: Prince Hamlet
cards.body: The prince of Denmark. Son of Gertrude and the recently deceased King Hamlet; nephew of the new king, Claudius.

cards.name: Claudius
cards.body: The new king of Denmark. Hamlet’s uncle, now married to Hamlet’s mother, Gertrude.

cards.name: Gertrude
cards.body: The queen of Denmark and Hamlet’s mother. Widow of the old king and now Claudius’s wife.

cards.name: Ophelia
cards.body: Polonius’s daughter and Laertes’s sister. Hamlet has been courting her.

cards.name: Polonius
cards.body: A senior adviser at the Danish court. Father of Ophelia and Laertes.

cards.name: Horatio
cards.body: Hamlet’s friend and a fellow student from Wittenberg.

cards.name: Laertes
cards.body: Polonius’s son and Ophelia’s brother.

cards.name: The Ghost
cards.body: The mysterious apparition seen by the watchmen at Elsinore.
cards.identityNote: Keep the identity uncertain at first. A later card may report its claim to be Hamlet’s father after Act 1 Scene 5; never announce the murder accusation from the first appearance.

cards.name: King Hamlet
cards.body: Denmark’s recently deceased king. Prince Hamlet’s father and Gertrude’s first husband.

cards.name: Rosencrantz
cards.body: A friend of Hamlet from his youth, usually seen with Guildenstern.

cards.name: Guildenstern
cards.body: A friend of Hamlet from his youth, usually seen with Rosencrantz.

cards.name: Young Fortinbras
cards.body: A Norwegian prince. His father lost lands to Hamlet’s father in single combat.

cards.name: The elder Fortinbras
cards.body: The Norwegian ruler defeated by King Hamlet. Father of the young Fortinbras.

cards.name: The King of Norway
cards.body: Young Fortinbras’s uncle, the elderly ruler of Norway.

cards.name: Barnardo
cards.body: A soldier keeping watch at Elsinore. He takes over Francisco’s midnight watch.

cards.name: Francisco
cards.body: A soldier on guard at Elsinore when the play opens. Barnardo comes to relieve him.

cards.name: Marcellus
cards.body: A soldier at Elsinore, keeping watch with Barnardo.

cards.name: Voltemand
cards.body: A Danish courtier sent with Cornelius as an envoy to Norway.

cards.name: Cornelius
cards.body: A Danish courtier who accompanies Voltemand on the mission to Norway.

cards.name: Reynaldo
cards.body: Polonius’s servant.

cards.name: The First Player
cards.body: An actor in the visiting company that Hamlet welcomes to Elsinore.

cards.name: The Player King
cards.body: The actor playing the king in the performance at court. A different figure from Claudius and Hamlet’s father.

cards.name: The Player Queen
cards.body: The actor playing the queen in the performance at court. A different figure from Gertrude.

cards.name: Lucianus
cards.body: A character in the play performed at court, introduced as the king’s nephew.

cards.name: The First Gravedigger
cards.body: The cemetery worker who jokes and debates while digging. Also labeled First Clown.

cards.name: The Second Gravedigger
cards.body: The First Gravedigger’s companion in the cemetery. Also labeled Second Clown.

cards.name: Osric
cards.body: An elaborately polite courtier at Elsinore.

cards.name: Yorick
cards.body: The late king’s jester, whom Hamlet knew as a child.

cards.name: Julius Caesar
cards.body: The Roman ruler invoked in Horatio’s comparison with ominous events in Denmark.

cards.name: Neptune
cards.body: The Roman god of the sea.
cards.editionNote: The opening modern-English passage explains the tides without naming Neptune; do not create a mention there.

cards.name: Jesus Christ
cards.body: The figure whose birth is celebrated at Christmas, referred to as the Saviour.
cards.editionNote: The opening modern-English passage says Christmas without naming the Saviour; do not create a mention there.

requiredReview: Reject the inherited global Hamlet alias: Act 1 Scene 1 paragraph 52 concerns his father, while paragraph 68 concerns the prince.
Distinguish elder and younger Fortinbras within the same speech. A paragraph-level override is insufficient.
KING and QUEEN speaker labels belong to Claudius/Gertrude or to the players according to scene and performance boundaries.
First-player and Player King may be the same performer, but actor and dramatic role are distinct lookup contexts, not additional people for gallery counts.
Validate which scene paragraph introduces each office, mission, or relationship. Basic identity may be supplied early; later assignments and concealed identity need gates.
Review cultural references throughout all 20 scenes before claiming complete reference coverage.
